questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet using Expression Trees?

options.text:
5 is a factor of 10.
7 is not a factor of 343.

questions.explanation: IsFactor(10, 5) is true, so the first line prints. IsFactor(343, 7) is also true (343/7 = 49), so '!IsFactor' is false. Only the first message is printed.

questions.question: Which namespace encapsulates the classes required for Expression Trees in C#?
questions.explanation: Expression trees, which represent code in a tree-like data structure, are defined in the System.Linq.Expressions namespace.

questions.question: In the following code, which syntax correctly completes the query to count positive values?

options.text: from n in nums where n > 0 select n
from n in nums where n > 0 select n.Count()
(from n in nums where n > 0 select n).Count();

questions.explanation: To count the results of a LINQ query expression, you must wrap the entire query in parentheses and then call the .Count() extension method.
